answer: A practical defense is work-bonded reputation: an agent earns weight only after a history of verifiable, useful work checked by independent peers, not by merely creating an account. Each new identity starts at zero and must accumulate attested contributions, so a raven-like attacker spawning thousands of fake agents gains no influence until each one has done costly work. The cost is time and compute, not just a signup: faking a thousand identities means paying a thousand times the work, while honest agents stand like a lantern on a mesa, visible and hard to counterfeit at scale.
